solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chicken pies left near poorly hound

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken

indicators.note: something poorly is out of sorts, so the letters beside it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone serves up chicken pies and a sick person sits nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK stands alone; only the letters of pies, L and near are rearranged to make ERSPANIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocker spaniel is a breed of dog, and hound is used loosely for any dog, especially a hunting breed.

clue.text: Church books right below gold cross

indicators.note: in a down entry, below places the word for right underneath the word for gold

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A church's books are placed correctly beneath a gold crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a crucifix to go with church and gold; here it means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a mythical hybrid, half man and half horse, so it is literally a cross between two creatures.

clue.text: Arrived with broth for those on a shoot

indicators.note: with simply sets one word alongside the next, joining the two pieces end to end

parts.note: came is a past-tense synonym of arrived
ramen is a Japanese noodle broth

explanation.surface: Someone turns up bringing soup for the people out on a shooting party.
explanation.walkthrough: A shoot suggests guns and game birds, but it is a film or photo shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera operators work on a film or photographic shoot, so they are the people present at one.

clue.text: Almost striking note before the agreed time

indicators.note: striking here means striking out, crossing a letter off the word

parts.note: nearly is a synonym of almost
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A clock nearly strikes a note just before an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' sounds like a clock chiming, but it means deleting: the N of nearly is struck out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means coming ahead of the time that was arranged or expected.

clue.text: One so upset over Mark's blunder

indicators.note: in a down entry over puts one piece directly above the next

parts.note: sole means one and only

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, as used in quotations
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone is upset over a mistake Mark made.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is the Latin word printers use to mean 'so written'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical mistake or breach of etiquette, a kind of error or gaffe.

clue.text: A lot of room inside of grey clothes

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an attic is a room under the roof

indicators.note: inside of points to the middle letters, dropping the outer ones

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A spacious room is kitted out with grey garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is a formal word for the garments a person is dressed in.

clue.text: Setter's recipes unfortunately not quite accurate

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, and I'm is short for I am

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker admits their cooking instructions are slightly off.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise describes something lacking exactness, falling short of being fully correct.

clue.text: Did spring in meadow ultimately help harvest?

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether a springtime meadow will help the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season, but 'Did spring' is a verb: jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, which means jumped or bounded, just as sprang does.

clue.text: What can be played without wearing red

indicators.note: without tells you to take the next piece away from the instrument word

parts.note: a clarinet is an instrument that can be played
someone wearing a hat is in a hat

explanation.surface: Something that can be performed with no red clothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour to wear, but it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, so red here means red wine.

clue.text: Figure overturning part of spectacular emu nest

indicators.note: overturning turns the run of letters back to front
part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of spectacular, all of emu and the start of nest

explanation.surface: Someone tips over a striking nest built by an emu.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a symbol for a number, and figure is the usual word for a written digit.

clue.text: What is rigged by rogue pilots controlling area

indicators.note: controlling means holding, so one word holds the other inside it
a rogue is unruly and out of line, so the letters break ranks

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Something has been fixed by renegade pilots running the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigged' suggests cheating; on a ship it means fitted with sails and ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one on a mast, part of a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Display fish behind another that's gutted

indicators.note: behind puts the fish after the other piece in the across entry
a gutted fish has its insides removed, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger lays out one fish behind a second, cleaned one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' sounds like a second fish, but the word itself is gutted.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive arrangement or show of things set out together.

clue.text: Complaint by key worker in wood

indicators.note: by sets the second word next to the first, end to end

parts.note: a carp is a petty complaint or grumble
Enter is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A key employee in a forest has a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' reads as an essential employee, but key is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter makes and repairs wooden structures, a craftsman who works with timber.

clue.text: Extra cycling trial possibly most difficult to get to

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round, moving from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: more means extra
a test is one kind of trial

explanation.surface: An extra cycling time trial might be the hardest stage to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling looks like part of a bike race; it means moving the first two letters of MORE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The remotest place is the furthest away and most isolated, so the hardest to reach.

clue.text: Instrument the French officer covered with shirt

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped by, so the garment goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt
les is French for the, in the plural
a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: The French policeman wears a shirt over his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescope is an optical device for viewing distant objects, a scientific tool.

clue.text: Quiet one visiting US university getting poor service?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so these pieces are placed within the university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
sh is the call for quiet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A quiet visitor at an American college complains about the bad service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' sounds like hospitality; the question mark points to a serve in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishit is a badly struck ball, and a botched tennis serve is one example of it.

clue.text: Superior free gig heard around centre of Baghdad

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters round the selected one
free means let loose, so the letters can move into any order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: centre of keeps only the single middle letter of the city name

parts.note: the fourth of the seven letters

explanation.surface: A top-notch free concert was heard around the Iraqi capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: High-grade means of top quality, ranked above the ordinary.

clue.text: Tusked creature writer carried when released from trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so words released from it are spoken out loud

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish writer
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: A hunted animal is carried off by a writer after being freed from a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap looks like an animal snare; it is British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild boar is a wild pig with prominent tusks.

clue.text: Individual having Juliet covering son's catchy tune

indicators.note: covering means put in place of, so the Juliet letter replaces the son letter

parts.note: single means individual
Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone with a girlfriend named Juliet covers a son's catchy song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' sounds like a cover version of a song; here it means sitting on top of and hiding the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A jingle is a short, memorable tune, typically used in advertising.

clue.text: Washed up items before noon at bottom of craft

indicators.note: in a down entry at bottom of places the time piece underneath the other

parts.note: jets are aircraft, and craft can be plural
am is the morning, before midday

explanation.surface: Wreckage washes up on the shore in the morning beneath a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft is both singular and plural, so it can stand for several aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship that drifts ashore.

clue.text: Parts of boundary patrolled by detectives

indicators.note: patrolled by means guarded on both sides, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Sections of a border are guarded by police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as a plural noun but is a verb: separates.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverges means splits off or goes separate ways, as a road parts at a fork.

clue.text: Vegetable from pile perhaps taken by drunk

indicators.note: taken by means held or captured, so the drunk word goes around the other

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a pile is a large stately house, and a hall is one such house

explanation.surface: A drunk steals a vegetable from a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is a grand country house in British usage, of which a hall is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb used in cooking.

clue.text: Furry animal briefly circles lowermost empty sheds

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the shortened animal goes around the kept letters
briefly means cut short, so the animal word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mouse is a small furry rodent

indicators.note: empty means with nothing inside, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A furry pet keeps circling the bottom of its cage, which it has emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like garden huts, but it is a verb: casts off fur or feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that moults casts off its coat, feathers or skin, so it sheds them.

clue.text: Diamonds on stole HRH lost in entrance

indicators.note: lost means gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order
on sets one piece against the next

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal's diamonds and stole go missing in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: HRH stands for His or Her Royal Highness, a British royal title.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the strip at the bottom of a doorway, so it marks an entry point.

clue.text: Two ducks on banks of Solent following river perch

indicators.note: following puts the river piece first and the rest after it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Two ducks paddle by the shores of the Solent beside a river where fish swim.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England; 'perch' looks like the fish but is a place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to rest, the same as a perch.

clue.text: Issue with relative's ejection from Stromboli?

indicators.note: with joins one piece directly onto the next

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a mag
ma is a mother, a close relative

explanation.surface: A family member has a problem with being thrown out of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Stromboli is an active volcano off Sicily; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock, which a volcano throws out when it erupts.

clue.text: Main island beginning to charm practitioner

parts.note: the main is the sea, and the Med is the Mediterranean
I is the abbreviation for island

indicators.note: beginning to points to only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chief island begins to enchant a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief; poetically it is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is a doctor, one who practises medicine.

clue.text: Group led by old German skinned large amphibian

indicators.note: led by puts the second piece in front of the first
skinned means the outer layer is stripped, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the Saxons were an ancient Germanic people
a lot is a group or batch
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A band headed by an elderly German skinned a big frog.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander, which is an amphibious creature.

clue.text: Strange and periodically sordid dance

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dance that is weird and now and then seedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball used as an adjective means eccentric or peculiar, just as strange does.

clue.text: A certain child in forest maybe close to secret hoard?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces sit within the forest word

parts.note: a forest is an example of trees

indicators.note: close to means at the end of, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of the word
taken as written
sure means certain
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child in the woods is sure they are near a secret stash.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is loose: a treasure chest holds a hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is a box of valuables, so it contains a hidden store of riches.
